newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed up 0.06 rupees at 42.70 to the dollar on Sunday in the kerb amid a rise in supply of the U.S. currency, but dealers said the rupee was likely to open steady on Monday.
"Most major players have opted to wait and see before taking any position," one dealer said, adding that low demand for dollars had prompted small investors to book dollar profits.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 to the dollar.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed unchanged at 6.80 percent.
